correctedCritiques.pro-fundamental-consciousness-ends-regre: Strongest feature: The reply directly identifies explanatory dependence in natural candidates assembled from reducible components and presents fundamental consciousness as an intelligible terminus instead of accepting indefinite regress. Principal limitation: It speculatively classifies a natural conscious foundation as composite while treating consciousness as fundamental without independently demonstrating why mentality alone qualifies for nondependent foundational status. Live burden: Jones must establish that the strongest natural alternative is necessarily composite or dependent, supply nonstipulative grounds for fundamental consciousness, and explain why comparably basic impersonal structure cannot terminate the regress. Locked score: The mixed band reflects central contact and a coherent regress strategy, substantially moderated by unstable classifications, speculative premises, selective stopping, incomplete alternative testing, and limited evidence favoring consciousness.
correctedCritiques.con-conscious-god-not-physical-theory: Strongest feature: The response clearly distinguishes a metaphysical God model from physical theories constructed through recognized principles, particles, fields, or laws, providing a focused diagnostic criterion. Principal limitation: Jones compares explanatory model construction methods rather than claiming God is literally a particle-level physical theory, so defeating that classification only partly contacts the methodological analogy and construes its purpose narrowly. Live burden: Jump must identify which epistemic safeguards are indispensable in theoretical physics and demonstrate that the metaphysical proposal lacks them, instead of relying exclusively on disciplinary classification. Locked score: The strong/competent band reflects clear criteria and responsive scientific pressure, moderated by an overbroad definition, limited charity, incomplete contact with the analogy, and modest evidential support for exhaustiveness.
